subject: Data export controls & legal hold for onboarding - playbook and evidence
messages:
From: Emma Stahl <emma.stahl@greenlinehealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@greenlinehealth.com
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Data export controls & legal hold for onboarding

Hi Connor / Laura,

Thanks for the quick onboarding kickoff earlier. A few items our security and legal teams asked us to clarify before we move to production: 

1) Data exports & legal hold: we need to confirm whether Redwood can implement a legal-hold (prevent deletion/export) for an account-level event without affecting availability. Specifically: can you hold PII-associated records on request for up to 18 months, and provide an audit trail showing the hold was applied/removed?

2) Cross-border transfers: which subprocessors may process user PII outside the EU/UK? We need the mechanism used for transfers (SCCs, adequacy decisions, explicit consent) and a short statement on whether any subprocessors trigger data localization exceptions.

3) KMS & key custody: for onboarding we'd like to know if customer-managed keys (CMK) are supported, and if an HSM-backed option exists. If CMK is not available, what are the compensating controls?

4) Evidence & artifacts: please send any dataflow diagrams, the current subprocessor list with processing purpose, SOC2 evidentiary summary, and the expected lead time to get those artifacts certified for our audit.

Attaching our onboarding checklist for your reference (Greenline_onboarding_checklist.xlsx). Can we do a 30-minute call next week to walk through these points?

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Stahl
Security Program Manager, Greenline Health
emma.stahl@greenlinehealth.com
+1 (415) 555-0183

--
(attachment: Greenline_onboarding_checklist.xlsx)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Emma Stahl <emma.stahl@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Data export controls & legal hold for onboarding

Hi Emma — thanks for the checklist and the clear set of asks. Quick answers up front, and I'll follow with attachments and a proposed call slot: 

- Legal hold: yes, we support account-level legal holds that prevent deletion and flag data for retention. Holds are logged and time-stamped; we can export the hold audit trail as CSV. There are two options: default Redwood-managed retention (configurable) or an addendum to lock retention at the account level.

- Cross-border transfers: most of our hosted infra is in multi-region cloud providers; some subprocessors (e.g., monitoring, CDN logs vendor) may process metadata in other regions. We use SCCs where required and maintain an export mapping spreadsheet.

- KMS: we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS integrations (customer uploads or rotates keys). We also offer HSM-backed key material for Dedicated/Private deployments. If CMK is not selected, we apply strict access controls, split-key custody for master keys, and per-request attestation logs.

- Evidence: attaching a short export playbook (redwood-export-playbook.pdf) and a subprocessor export list. SOC2 summary can be provided — Marcus will attach the high-level package in the morning.

Call: I have Tue 6 Apr 10:00-10:30am PDT or Wed 7 Apr 2:00-2:30pm PDT. Which works?

Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0120

--
(attachment: redwood-export-playbook.pdf)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Emma Stahl <emma.stahl@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 08:15:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Data export controls & legal hold for onboarding

Emma — looping in a bit more detail from the privacy/product side. I wanted to be explicit about the artifacts you can expect: 

- Subprocessor export list: attached (subprocessors_export_sheet.csv). It contains subprocessors, processing purpose, and country of processing. If you need contractual subprocessors changes, we can escalate via our DPA addendum process.

- Dataflow diagram: public read-only link here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRedwoodDataFlows (contains redacted sequence diagrams, ingress/egress points, and where PII is stored vs ephemeral).

- KMS options: see attached (kms_options_overview.pdf). TL;DR: customer-managed keys supported for Hosted via Cloud KMS integrations (Bring-Your-Own-Key), Dedicated offers HSM-backed KMS with split-key custody, and Private installs can use customer HSMs. We maintain per-request key usage logs and can provide an export for audit.

- Legal hold implementation details: holds are applied at dataset/account scope; they prevent automated deletion and mark records for manual review. Holds are visible in the Console under Admin > Retention & Legal Hold. Removing a hold requires a two-person approval for accounts under enterprise contracts.

Marcus — attaching the SOC2 summary package (soc2-summary.pdf) for Emma and Legal. Connor — happy to join the call if needed.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Product Compliance, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

--
(attachments: subprocessors_export_sheet.csv, kms_options_overview.pdf, soc2-summary.pdf)

From: Emma Stahl <emma.stahl@greenlinehealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@greenlinehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 14:42:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Data export controls & legal hold for onboarding

Hi Laura / Connor — this is very helpful, thank you. A few follow-ups from Legal / Security after review: 

- SOC2: the summary is fine for scoping, but Legal will request the SOC2 Type II report under NDA. Can you confirm the typical lead time to get that signed NDA and the report delivered?

- Legal hold scope: confirm that holds do not inhibit ability to snapshot for backup / DR and that Redwood will provide a CSV extract of held records on request (format and fields to be agreed). We may need an addendum specifying preservation scope.

- Subprocessors: as part of our procurement we need a signed acknowledgment if any subprocessor performs PII processing in APAC and whether APAC processing includes identifiable user content or only telemetry/metrics. The CSV is a great start — can you add a brief "processing type" column (identifiable_content | pseudonymized | telemetry) and re-share?

- Next steps: let's take Tue 6 Apr 10:00am PDT for the 30-minute call. I'll invite a legal rep to the meeting (you'll see an updated calendar invite). Also linking our HubSpot opportunity for tracking: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234560/company/98765

Thanks — Emma
Emma Stahl
Security Program Manager, Greenline Health
